_comment: D33 selective-revocation wire manifest. Live scenarios (keys not starting with '_') are cold-judged by the REAL RevocationEngine on every gate run: the claimant's asserted post-revocation verdicts must match the engine's recomputed verdicts exactly. Zero live scenarios = explicit DORMANT, never a false green. Keys starting with '_' are worked examples only — documentation of the fraud this law exists to prevent and of the honest case — never judged live. To activate a scenario, copy an example to a live key and set 'asserted' to the claimed verdicts; a wrong claim blocks the PR (exit 1).

_example._note: THE FRAUD. Claim C: (E1^E3) v (E2^E4) v (E3^E4)[staging]. E1 revoked — but E2 was secretly derived from E1, so the E2^E4 path was never independent. The naive checker asserts REQUALIFIED over the full scope. The real engine DOWNGRADEs C to staging-only. Registered as a live claim, this scenario exits 1 VIOLATION naming asserted=REQUALIFIED actual=DOWNGRADED.

_example_honest._note: THE HONEST CASE. Same scenario, but E2 is genuinely independent (no derivation edge). The engine REQUALIFies C over the full scope and leaves D UNAFFECTED — the asserted verdicts below are what the engine actually recomputes. Registered as a live claim, this scenario exits 0 PASS.
